text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"Large trials in vitamin D-replete adults found no effect of vitamin D supplementation on cancer, cardiovascular events, type 2 diabetes, bone density or falls.","cited_pids":["fbce4d7a6120#3"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"The Finnish trial found no lower rates of major cardiovascular events or invasive cancer in older adults taking vitamin D.","cited_pids":["0dafa2c8c11c#3"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"The VITAL trial found no reduction in fracture risk with vitamin D supplementation among generally healthy midlife and older adults not selected for deficiency.","cited_pids":["d8b33533d51c#3"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"A meta-analysis found that vitamin D supplementation did not reduce all-cause mortality but reduced cancer death by 16%.","cited_pids":["81282aae0b32#2"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"The US Preventive Services Task Force recommends against vitamin D supplementation for fracture prevention in healthy postmenopausal women.","cited_pids":["9c98e4515e3d#0"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"The Endocrine Society suggests empiric vitamin D supplementation for adults aged 75 and older.","cited_pids":["8279771cfc3d#4"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"The Endocrine Society suggests empiric vitamin D supplementation for people with high-risk prediabetes.","cited_pids":["8279771cfc3d#4"]},{"cid":"c8","text":"Some evidence suggests that deficient individuals or prediabetic patients may benefit from long-term vitamin D supplementation.","cited_pids":["58487bc44db2#1"]},{"cid":"c9","text":"Routine daily vitamin D use is not clearly supported for generally healthy adults.","cited_pids":[]}]}
